To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chemotherapy, especially alkylating agents, is associated with a 5- to 10-fold increased risk of early menopause, that the risk of menopause is highest after treatment with MOPP, that the risk is related to cumulative dose of procarbrazine, and that time to premature menopuse is longer after treatment at early ages.
treatment of HL with alkylating agents is associated with an increased risk of premature (early) menopause.
chemotherapy is associated with a significantly increased risk of premature ovarian insufficiency compared with radiotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cancer treatments on female fertility and reproductive health.
a better understanding of the risk of premature ovarian failure in women treated for Hodgkin lymphoma and the factors that determine the occurrence of this adverse effect.
the treatment-related risk factors for the premature menopause following the Hodgkin's lymphoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the risk for premature menopause after treatment for HL is strongly related to the use of alkylating agents, and that the risk is increased in women receiving MOPP-based chemotherapy, especially when procarbazine is used.
the risk of menopause is high in women treated for Hodgkin lymphoma, and is related to age at treatment, the use of alkylating agents and the dose.

the risk of premature ovarian failure is increased after treatment for HL, but the magnitude of the risk varies considerably with the specific treatment regimen, the cumulative dose of alkylating agents, and the age at treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk of premature ovarian failure in women treated with chemotherapy for HL is strongly associated with the cumulative dose of alkylating agents and procarbazine in particular.
chemotherapy is the most important treatment factor for premature menopause.
the risk of premature ovarian failure in young women with Hodgkin lymphoma is strongly associated with cumulative doses of alkylating agents and with MOPP-based regimens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of premature ovarian insufficiency is high among women treated for HL, and is strongly associated with the use of alkylating agents.
premature menopause is a serious adverse effect of treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma that can have a major impact on quality of life and fertility.
premature menopause is an important long-term adverse treatment effect in women cured from HL, which should be considered in clinical trials and in counseling women before starting treatment.
